title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Administrative Cases concerning Disclosure of Government Information

articles.content_en:
Article 2 Where a citizen, legal person, or any other organization considers that an administrative organ fails to perform its duty of proactively disclosing government information according to law and directly initiates an action to the People's Court, it shall be informed that it shall first apply to the administrative organ for access to government information.
Where a party is dissatisfied with such acts as the administrative organ's reply or failure to reply within the time limit, it may apply for administrative reconsideration or initiate an administrative action according to law.

Article 3 A citizen, legal person, or any other organization that initiates an action on the grounds that acts of the administrative organ such as disclosing or refusing to disclose government information infringe upon its lawful rights and interests shall fall within the scope of "citizens, legal persons, or other organizations with an interest" as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 25 of the Administrative Procedure Law.

Article 4 Where a citizen, legal person, or any other organization initiates an action against an act of proactively disclosing government information, the administrative organ that disclosed the government information shall be the defendant.
Where a citizen, legal person, or any other organization initiates an action against an act of disclosing government information upon application, the administrative organ that made the reply shall be the defendant; if no reply is made within the time limit, the administrative organ that received the application shall be the defendant.
In accordance with Article 4 of the Regulations on the Disclosure of Government Information, where a local people's government at or above the county level designates a government information disclosure working institution to be responsible for the daily work of government information disclosure of that organ, and a citizen, legal person, or any other organization initiates an action against an act of government information disclosure performed by such institution in its own name, that institution shall be the defendant.

Article 6 Where the defendant claims that the information applied for by the plaintiff is a state secret and refuses to disclose it, and provides classification markings, a duration of secrecy, or other evidentiary materials, the People's Court shall uphold such claim.
Where the defendant claims that disclosure of the government information applied for by the plaintiff may endanger national security, public security, or social stability, and provides evidence of the potential adverse effects of such disclosure or makes a reasonable explanation, the People's Court shall uphold such claim.
Where the People's Court finds upon trial that disclosure of the government information may endanger national security, public security, or social stability, it shall have the authority to require the parties to provide or supplement evidence.

Article 8 When trying a first-instance case concerning government information disclosure, the People's Court may apply summary procedures.
When trying a case concerning government information disclosure, the People's Court shall adopt appropriate trial methods depending on the circumstances, so as to avoid divulging government information involving state secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, or government information that is required to be kept confidential by laws, regulations, or relevant state provisions.

Article 9 Where government information is kept by the defendant's archival institution or archival staff, the relevant provisions of the Regulations on the Disclosure of Government Information shall apply.
Where archives involving matters of government information disclosure have been transferred to the state archives at various levels, the matter shall be handled in accordance with laws, regulations, and relevant state provisions on archives management.

Article 13 Before the government information has been disclosed, where the plaintiff initiates an action requesting the defendant not to disclose the government information, and the People's Court finds upon trial that the government information involves the plaintiff's trade secrets or personal privacy and that non-disclosure will not cause substantial adverse effects on public interest, the People's Court shall order the defendant not to disclose the government information.
During the proceedings, where the plaintiff applies for the suspension of disclosure of government information involving its trade secrets or personal privacy, and the People's Court finds upon trial that the requirements of Article 56 of the Administrative Procedure Law are met, it shall rule to temporarily suspend disclosure.

Article 15 This Interpretation shall come into force on June 1, 2025.
Upon the coming into force of this Interpretation, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases concerning the Disclosure of Government Information (Fa Shi [2011] No. 17) shall be abolished simultaneously. Any judicial interpretations and normative documents previously issued by the Supreme People's Court that are inconsistent with this Interpretation shall no longer apply.
